text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Sunday it would launch a new traded share investment on the Australian Stock Exchange which would combine the advantages of a geared investment with a high fully-franked yield.

Macquarie said the new product, NAB instalments, was based on an investment in the ordinary shares of National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB). It would allow investors to partly pay for an investment in NAB stock while still receiving the full amount of dividends on the underlying share, including any franking credits.
"NAB instalments offer a simple listed alternative to margin lending and other forms of gearing," Macquarie executive director Ottmar Weiss said in a statement.
"Instalments allow investors to obtain exposure to a blue chip investment for a relatively small outlay - with no margin calls and no obligation to outlay money for the second instalment," he said.
Weiss said investors could invest in NAB instalments by paying the first instalment upon subscription, with a minimum investment of A$2,250.
The first instalment would include a prepaid interest component which may be tax deductible, depending on an individual's circumstances.
The second instalment would be determined over a five-business day period around the close of the offer and would be payable 13 months later.
During the term of the NAB instalments, the NAB shares would be held in trust with all dividends, including franking credits, paid to the investor.
Upon payment of the final instalment, the NAB shares would be transferred to the investor.
The Australian Stock Exchange said in a separate statement that it had approved the NAB instalments for listing on the exchange's warrants market.
Macquarie said the applications for the investment would open on December 2 and were expected to close on December 13.
